_: Fixtures for the match-quote guard. Every sentence below is VERBATIM from a
real Form 5500 audit attachment in the live store; `expect` is the verdict a
human review of that filing gives. Two implementations must agree on all of
them: scripts/lib-quote.mjs (canonical) and the browser twin in app.js.
evaluates the second in the real page. The rule drifted between its two homes
once already, which is the whole reason this file exists.
hasFormula = whether an extracted formula is displayed above the quote, which
changes the question from 'is this the formula?' to 'is this about the match?'

cases.text: The Company makes safe-harbor matching contributions equal to 100% of deferrals of the first 3% of eligible compensation, then 50% of deferrals on the next 2% of eligible compensation.

cases.why: rate and connector NOT adjacent: '(50%) of'
cases.text: The Company makes matching contributions equal to fifty percent (50%) of eligible compensation that a participant contributes, with a maximum matching contribution of $2,400 per year.

cases.why: lead-in phrasing, 'equal to a 100% match on'
cases.text: The Company provides a safe harbor matching contribution equal to a 100% match on the participant's contributions with an elective deferral percentage less than or equal to 1%.
During the year ended December 31, 2024, the Plan Documents required Company safe harbor matching contributions up to four percent of eligible compensation for non-highly compensated employees.

cases.why: dollar cap made a rate by a period
cases.text: The Company makes a dollar-per-dollar matching contribution of up to a maximum of $500 per year for each participant.

cases.why: no number at all — cannot be a formula
cases.text: They may select from among several funds in which to invest their contributions, employer matching contributions and profit-sharing contributions.

cases.why: the number belongs to 'vested', not to the match
cases.text: The Company matching contributions vest 20% annually until the participant is 100% vested at the end of five years.

cases.why: bare 'each' must not turn a vesting rate into a match rate
cases.text: Employer matching contributions and employer profit sharing contributions, plus any earnings they generate, vest at 20% each year starting year one and are fully vested after five years.
Each participant's account is credited with the participant's contributions, the Company's matching contributions, and the allocation of Plan earnings.
Any pre-tax and/or Roth (after-tax) contributions made prior to completing 12 months of service are not eligible for the company matching contribution.

cases.why: a YEAR'S TOTAL in dollars is not a rate — El Valor published this as a formula
cases.text: There were $29,342 and $23,639 of employer matching contributions for the years ended December 31, 2024 and 2023, respectively.

cases.why: one sentence used as evidence for both; leading word settles it
cases.text: Vesting - At any time, participants are 100% vested in their contributions, the Company's matching contributions and any amounts rolled over to the Plan.

cases.why: discretionary match states no number; it is still the right evidence
cases.text: The Company may make a discretionary matching contribution.

cases.why: same sentence cannot STAND ALONE as the formula
cases.text: The Company may make a discretionary matching contribution.

cases.why: off-subject even beneath a parsed formula
cases.text: Participants become 100% vested in employer matching contributions after six years and employer discretionary contributions after three years of service.
